app.title: Shadow Lamp
app.subtitle: Lamp shades that project your image · STL for printing
app.description: Design lamp shades that project your image as a shadow and export them as STL for 3D printing.

image.title: Image
image.hint: Use black and white images. SVG gives cleaner edges; transparent areas count as white.
image.readError: The image could not be read

interpretation.title: Interpretation
interpretation.label: Black areas of the image will be
interpretation.hintLight: Black areas get lit: the lamp cuts them out as holes.
interpretation.hintShadow: Black areas stay in shadow: the lamp covers them with material.

position.title: Position on the wall
position.dragHint: Drag the image across the wall in the 3D view. Outside the image, the camera orbits as usual.

lamp.rimHint: The rim grows to cover the lip of the base and cap ({lip} mm + 1 mm).

bulb.title: Bulb
bulb.note: The bulb sits {depth} cm inside the shade. Holes are angled toward it so the wall thickness doesn't clip the shadow. A small LED gives sharper edges.

bridges.title: Bridges
bridges.hint: Bridges hold parts that would otherwise fall out (like the middle of an “O”).

partsTab.title: Snap-fit parts
partsTab.toggleHint: The base goes against the wall and holds the hollow bulb post (the cable runs inside). The cap closes the room side.
partsTab.clearanceHint: Gap between the lip and the shade. More clearance = looser fit.

export.coarsened: · cell enlarged to {cell} mm due to size
export.error: The STL could not be generated: {message}

viewer.moveImageTitle: Drag the image across the wall with the mouse

cap.title: Cap
cap.lithoHint: The cap shows your logo when the lamp is on: the room side is flat and, on the inside, steps get thicker with darker tones.
cap.glow: How it will look when lit
cap.minFeatureHint: Smooths the image and removes details smaller than this (≈ 2 × nozzle).
cap.printNote: Total thickness {total} mm. Print it lying flat, flat face on the bed, with a layer height that divides {step} mm (e.g. 0.2).
cap.hotspot: The bulb is {gap} mm from the cap: the center will look brighter. Aim for at least {min} mm (move the bulb toward the wall or make the shade longer).

project.unsaved: There are changes not saved to a file
project.saveTitle: Save the project to a .shadelamp file (Ctrl+S · Ctrl+Shift+S to save as)
project.openError: Could not open the file. Is it a .shadelamp project?
project.confirmDiscard: There are changes not saved to a file. Continue and discard them?
project.restored: Your last design was restored (saved automatically in this browser).

memory.title: Save your project often
memory.text: This app uses a lot of memory (with large images it can exceed 3–4 GB). If you leave the tab in the background, the browser may reload it to free memory. Your design is saved automatically in this browser, but the safest option is to use “Save”.

discarded.title: The browser reloaded this tab
discarded.text: It was closed in the background to free memory. Your design was restored from the autosave; to not depend on it, use “Save” and keep the .shadelamp file.

welcome.title: Welcome to Shadow Lamp
welcome.text: Here you design a lamp shade to 3D print. It has holes calculated so that, when the bulb is on, the light draws your image on the wall. Here are the basics in one minute.

image.title: Choose your image
image.text: Upload a black and white drawing (PNG, JPG or SVG) or drag it here. Simple, large shapes like a logo or a silhouette work best. You can start with the sample image.

interpretation.title: Light or shadow?
interpretation.text: Decide what happens to the black parts of your image: “Light” cuts them out as holes (they light up on the wall) and “Shadow” keeps them covered with material.

viewer.title: See the result
viewer.text: In the 3D view, drag to rotate and use the mouse wheel to zoom. Turn on “Wall light” to see the image projected as it will look with the lamp on.

tabs.title: Adjust the lamp
tabs.text: In “Lamp” you change the shape, the size and where the bulb goes. In “Bridges” you hold the parts that would fall out (like the center of an “O”). In “Parts” you generate the base, cap and post to assemble it.

export.title: Download to print
export.text: Choose which parts to export and the quality, and download the STL files. Open them in your 3D printing software (Cura, PrusaSlicer, Bambu Studio…).

project.title: Save your project
project.text: “Save” creates a .shadelamp file with your whole design, images included; “Open” brings it back whenever you want. The browser may reload the tab if it stays in the background, so save often (Ctrl+S).

done.title: Ready to start!
done.text: You can see it again at any time with the “Tutorial” button at the bottom right of the 3D view.

donate.title: Support the project
